NPLify · P0 Technical Baseline

Deliverable 1 — Entity-Relationship Diagram & Data Model · Draft v5.7

New XP Technologies Limited

11 October 2026 · Confidential · Internal baseline document

Status and conventions

Status: Draft v5.7 (11 October 2026) is v5.6 plus D46, the ledger design agreed with NPL on 10–11 October (variance by cause, loss booked to NPL first, accruals at conversion, NPL-GR's two invoices with the remittance markup absorbing partner cost and forex, earnings kept unconverted and offset between partners, the promise discharged on release, fee parts on the principal): two tables, three views, invariants 40–44. Draft v5.6 (9 October 2026) was v5.5 with personal names removed from every example and attribution; v5.5 closed the 8–9 October work, consolidating v5.3 and v5.4 and carrying every decision to D45 — a CLIENT parent above PROJECT with a client-level roll-up (D38), NPL's operational answers (D39–D41), the quote-validity extensions and the honoured expired rate (D45, replacing D42), the reporting currency and one system-settings area with ROLE and ROLE_RIGHT (D43, D44). It applies the thirteen fee-practice decisions D20–D32, the same-currency rule D33 the three FRS-term decisions D34–D36 and the naming alignment D37, confirmed by NPL on 8–9 October from the fee table, NPL’s workbook answers and the Project Context and Payment methods tabs: volume tiers and per-sender splits (D20, D21), the customer-facing fee (D22), NPL-GR as an own-desk project (D23), invoices paid in parts (D24), a rounding menu (D25), markup shared with a client party and rebates as their own stream (D26, D27), partner rates as quoted (D28), the bank cutoff and rate lock (D29), cash by token with rates per city (D30), wallet screening (D31), single-use accounts and loss events (D32), and same-currency pass-through (D33). Fourteen tables and five views are added; invariants 3 and 9 are restated; invariants 20–39 are new. NPL’s answers to the operational questions of 9 October are applied as D39–D41, the quote-validity extensions and the honoured expired rate as D45 (replacing D42), the system reporting currency as D43 and the single system-settings area (roles, settings, platform pairs) as D44. The amendments of 9 October (D15 closed, D27, D29) the evening additions D34–D36 (holiday calendar, quote package, message template — the FRS terms that had no home) and the naming alignment D37 are recorded in §6. It carries v5.0–v5.2 (D13–D19) unchanged. Supersedes v5.5, v5.4 and v5.3 (the working drafts of 8–9 October), v5.2, v5.1, v5.0 and v4.0 in full. This baseline is an internal New XP document; the client deliverables are derived from it. Dependent documents have not yet been regenerated against this version (see §6).

Convention: all monetary amounts are stored as exact decimals; every table carries created_at / created_by; audit, approvals and locking are modelled once (domain 4) and apply to all master data. Derived figures (client balance, group entitlement, offsets, custody) are views over postings and deals — never stored.

Seven diagrams across four domains, one schema: 70 tables and 12 views. In each diagram, entities defined in another diagram appear with no attributes and name that diagram. Relationship lines run from the referenced row to the row that stores the foreign key; ||--o{ is composition (the parent owns the child), ||..o{ a reference or a polymorphic link resolved by a type column plus an id. Diagram 3a of v5.2 is split in v5.3 because the deal leg and its stamps outgrew one page: 3a is the deal and its collection, 3b the conversion and its exceptions, and the settlement diagram (3b in v5.2) becomes 3c. Section 6 lists what changed since v4.0; Appendix A reconciles the model with the FRS; Appendix B is the data dictionary.

1 · Configuration domain

A Client is the commercial relationship NPL contracts with; a Project is one arrangement with it (D38) and owns its configuration. Partners are global counterparties; how a partner is used in this project is the partner configuration block — fees, vehicles, endpoints, destination approvals and rebate terms hang off it. Counterparty receivers are organised in receiver groups, the unit entitlement is tracked on, and each receiving entity holds one or more accounts with a currency and rail.

Diagram 1a. PARTNER_CONFIG, PARTNER_PAIR, DESTINATION_APPROVAL, FEE_STRUCTURE are defined in Diagram 1b.

Diagram 1b. PROJECT, CURRENCY_PAIR, SENDER, RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT, OWN_WALLET are defined in Diagram 1a.

Notes

  • A Client is the commercial relationship NPL contracts with; a Project is one arrangement with it (D38) and owns its configuration. Counterparty receivers sit in receiver groups: every project has one default group and every counterparty receiver belongs to exactly one group. Entitlement is tracked per group, so payouts within a group are ordinary settlement and only payouts across groups are offsets; a project with a single group never has an offset.
  • A Receiver has a kind: counterparty for a client receiver; sender_return stands for a sender so refunds use the ordinary payout path and the partner's destination approval; partner_transit stands for a partner's collection endpoint so the hop of a two-leg route is an ordinary payout. sender_return and partner_transit receivers belong to no group (group_id is null). They never appear on forward deals or allow lists — both validate kind = counterparty — and a payout to them is attributed to the group of the leg that pays them, so no entitlement moves between groups on a refund or a hop. Groups exist for entitlement and offset accounting; refund exclusion is a receiver-kind rule, not a group (D13).
  • A receiving entity holds one or more accounts, each with a currency and rail (EUR via SWIFT and EUR via SEPA are two accounts). An account is a bank account or a wallet (account_kind): a bank account carries bank_details_ref and a bank rail; a wallet carries network and address explicitly, mirroring the partner-side COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT, so addresses can be checksum-validated, checked against the rail, and found when the same address is registered with two partners. Destination approvals and settlement lines point at the account. No table stores actual bank details: bank_details_ref points at the external store.
  • Fees are per partner × pair (FEE_STRUCTURE under PARTNER_PAIR), so choosing the partner is part of pricing. PARTNER.disclosure_style records whether the partner's markup is visible; partner_fee_pct is known only for fee_on_market partners.
  • A partner operates through one or more legal vehicles (PARTNER_ENTITY: PT-tour, PT Global Inc); the deal stamps the vehicle at quote so paperwork names the right company. Each vehicle owns the endpoints a sender can pay into (COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT): kind = bank with a currency and bank_details_ref, or kind = wallet with network and address. The partner side therefore mirrors the client side — PARTNER_CONFIG → PARTNER_ENTITY → COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT as RECEIVER → RECEIVING_ENTITY → RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT (D15). An endpoint also carries a nullable rail: a bank endpoint must have it before it becomes active, and a wallet may leave it null but must match network when it is set (D18); the endpoint's kind must match the leg's collection_method (D19). Cash-in has no endpoint record; the leg carries the city and the collection the token (D30). The collected cash amount is rounded by the pair's cash_rounding option — truncate, nearest or round up — to cash_rounding_unit (100 / 500 / 1,000 by currency), the same menu as payout rounding (D25).
  • Destination approval is per partner: DESTINATION_APPROVAL is an account of the project's receiving entity as registered with this partner, carrying the partner's approval status and the payout details the partner holds. Those details follow the account's kind: bank_details_ref for a bank account, network and address for a wallet (D16). SETTLEMENT_SENDING_ENTITY is the narrative on an outgoing transfer; SETTLEMENT_RAIL is the bank/EMI that executes it; neither holds money. COLLECTION_SENDING_ENTITY is provenance only and never a payout destination.
  • OWN_WALLET has a role: reroute contingency (AQN-LT-Sub at Aquanow), own desk, or a collection bridge on a network a partner lacks, forwarded to the partner as a hop within the wallet's custody limit (D40); PARTNER_CONFIG.applicable_for_reroute defines the alternate-partner set. PARTNER.supported_methods declares what a partner offers — cash and local deposits have no standing endpoint to read it from (D39). WALLET_REGISTRY lists every known address with its owner and role. Under an own-desk partner configuration (is_own_desk, the NPL-GR game-reseller project) NPL itself is the converting party: its pairs are priced market plus NPL's markup and its collection endpoints are NPL's own wallets (COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT.own_wallet_id); the custody view reports every such balance (D23).
  • Fees in v5.3. A FEE_OVERRIDE may carry its own sender / receiver split instead of inheriting the structure's proportion (D20). FEE_TIER rows under a structure price by the project's calendar-month volume; a leg that takes the month past a threshold is split across two tiers (D21). customer_facing_fee_basis / customer_facing_fee_pct on the structure say what the customer's quote prints when it differs from the recorded parts; the printed "source rate" is derived at quote, never typed (D22). CURRENCY_PAIR.amount_rounding is a menu — truncate, nearest or round up, to the unit or to rounding_unit — and a pair may have the same currency on both sides (D25, D33).
  • Who else earns on a deal. MARKUP_SHARE_PARTY / MARKUP_SHARE_RULE record a share NPL pays — or, with basis share_of_net_markup and party_kind client_party, the customer who provides a sub-account and shares NPL's markup (Raeen): the base is the leg's fee parts less its partner cost, rebates excluded, several parties may hold rules with different shares, and settlement_mode party_retains means the party holds the converted money and pays NPL the remainder monthly (D26). PARTNER_REBATE_RULE records the rebate a partner pays NPL, with a basis (percentage of amount or of the partner's fee) and an optional scope by sender or fee structure; the rebate is NPL's alone and is reported as its own stream (D27).
  • Cutoff, screening, single use. PARTNER.bank_cutoff_time (the partner's own clock, beside its rate expiry and holiday calendar), its per-day changes in PARTNER_CUTOFF_OVERRIDE (an agreed extension or an early close) and PARTNER_PAIR.needs_bank_lock drive same-day or next-day conversion and, on bank rails, same-day or next-day settlement (D29). Cash legs carry their city (DEAL.cash_location) and cash rate versions theirs (D30). WALLET_SCREENING records the screening of a sending or receiving wallet address, by Operations, and the endpoint's risk_band says which decisions may land on it (D31). An endpoint or a receiving-entity account may be single_use, reserved for one deal (ad hoc local deposit accounts, D32). HOLIDAY rows under the partner are the dates behind every "next business day" (D34); MESSAGE_TEMPLATE is the versioned wording of outgoing messages and declares the fields it may print — a quote template prints sender-facing figures only (D36).

2 · Rates domain

Diagram 2. RATE_SOURCE, CURRENCY_PAIR are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_PAIR in 1b; DEAL in 3a; CONVERSION, BALANCE_CONVERSION in 3b.

Notes

  • The rate comparison for the day is created lazily by the first deal that needs it, one per partner × pair × date, and reused by every deal that day. A partner may give a new rate during the day, so one date can hold several versions. Rolling averages are built from confirmed versions only.
  • A version is breached when spread > avg_2w × (1 + variance_threshold_rel); quoting and conversion on that partner × pair freeze until Finance approves with a reason, rejects, or asks for a better rate. Versions are never overwritten; every deal leg, conversion and balance conversion references its exact version.
  • Cross-source slippage is a query over MARKET_RATE across sources for the same pair and window.
  • A version stores the rate as the partner quoted it (quoted_rate, quoted_direction); rate is normalised to the pair's direction and derived — 1 ÷ quoted when the directions differ — so Ali's 1.1738 becomes 0.851934 without a hand inversion, and a direction slip is caught by the breach check (D28). Cash pairs are priced per location: INR cash in Delhi and in Mumbai are two versions on the same day (D30).

Derived views (never stored)

ViewDefinition
PROJECT_BALANCE(project, partner, currency)PROJECT_BALANCE(project, partner, currency) — the client’s money resting at one partner for one project (was CLIENT_BALANCE until v5.4, renamed because CLIENT now exists and CLIENT_POSITION is the client-level roll-up, D38) = Σ conversions’ actual_out booked at that partner (deal legs and balance conversions, target side) − Σ balance conversions’ amount_in (source side) + Σ returned amounts − Σ released settlement totals. Carries rounding dust below one unit. v5.3 (D29): also reports a pending column — the expected_out of legs whose rate is locked with the partner but whose money has not yet been collected or converted; a void removes it. Pending is never a posting.
GROUP_ENTITLEMENT(group, currency)GROUP_ENTITLEMENT(group, currency) = Σ client_net of converted legs (forward and return) attributed to the group ± entitlement re-attributions − Σ SETTLEMENT_LINE.amount on lines whose settling deal is attributed to the group + Σ returned amounts on those lines. A payout to a group-less receiver debits the group of the leg that pays it, read from SETTLEMENT_LINE.deal_id (v5.0 D13; D17 makes the paying leg a stored column). Σ over a project's groups = Σ PROJECT_BALANCE over partners, per currency.
OFFSET(group, currency)OFFSET(group, currency) = GROUP_ENTITLEMENT; positive = owed, negative = holding another group's flow. Arises only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to another group (v5.0); zero by construction in a single-group project. Carries Management approval and tighter aging.
CUSTODY(own_wallet)CUSTODY(own_wallet) = Σ collections into the own wallet under open reroutes + Σ recovered dues resting there + Σ own-desk client balances (D23) + Σ bridge collections not yet forwarded (D40) − Σ forwarded or paid out; each row with deal, reason, role and age. The standing control on money in NPL’s hands.
INVOICE_BALANCE(invoice)INVOICE_BALANCE(invoice) = INVOICE.amount − Σ SETTLEMENT_LINE.obligation_discharged over lines with outcome confirmed. The open part of a vendor obligation paid in another currency, in parts (v5.3, D24).
PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME(project, month, currency)PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME(project, month, currency) = Σ DEAL.amount_in over forward legs of the project collected in the calendar month, in the tier’s volume currency. Read at quote to choose the FEE_TIER; stamped on the leg as tier_volume_basis (v5.3, D21).
CLIENT_POSITION(client, currency)CLIENT_POSITION(client, currency) = Σ over the client’s projects of PROJECT_BALANCE (per partner), GROUP_ENTITLEMENT, CUSTODY, and the period’s earnings (EARN_GROSS) and rebates (EARN_REBATE) from postings — the client-level report that project = client made impossible. Compared with CLIENT.exposure_ceiling when set (v5.4, D38). Its one-currency total is a REPORTING_VALUE, an estimate at the latest market rate (D43).
WALLET_REGISTRY(network, address)WALLET_REGISTRY(network, address) = every wallet address the model knows, with its owner and role: the partners’ receiving wallets (COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT kind wallet, with risk_band), NPL’s own wallets (OWN_WALLET with role), receivers’ wallets (RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT kind wallet, with their DESTINATION_APPROVALs) and the sender addresses seen in WALLET_SCREENING with their latest decision. A view, never a second copy of an address: it answers which networks a partner accepts, which wallet is the bridge, and whether an address was seen before under another owner — the FRS ‘wallet registry’ (v5.4, D40).
REPORTING_VALUE(subject, currency, as_of)REPORTING_VALUE(subject, currency, as_of) = any per-currency figure of the model — a PROJECT_BALANCE, a CLIENT_POSITION line, a month’s collection volume (PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME), earnings and rebates from postings, custody — multiplied by the latest MARKET_RATE of the platform pair for that currency (its PAIR_RATE_SOURCE chain), with the market_rate_id and captured_at it used and a stale flag when the rate is older than reporting_rate_max_age_min. An estimate for display: the figures in each currency stay the facts, the converted total is a view over them at the moment it is read (v5.4, D43). Serves project-level and overall collection volumes, earnings and current balances in one currency.
RESELLER_MARGIN(resale_invoice)RESELLER_MARGIN(resale invoice) = RESALE_INVOICE.amount − VENDOR_INVOICE.amount, in the invoice currency, equal to RESELL_REVENUE − RESELL_COST posted for the pair: NPL-GR’s game reseller revenue, fixed when the two invoices are posted and untouched by anything the remittance side does (v5.7, D46).
REMITTANCE_MARGIN(deal)REMITTANCE_MARGIN(deal) = EARN_GROSS (net of markup shares) − EXP_PARTNER ± VAR_FX_TIMING − EXP_BANKFEE − EXP_NETWORK − EXP_ROUNDING on the deal’s postings, in the converted currency: NPL’s remittance earnings on one deal, including the forex result of instalments paid at different days’ rates (v5.7, D46).
NPL_PROFIT(scope, period, currency)NPL_PROFIT(scope, period, currency) = remittance earnings (EARN_GROSS + EARN_REBATE − EXP_PARTNER − EXP_BANKFEE − EXP_NETWORK − EXP_ROUNDING − EXP_LOSS ± VAR_CONVERSION ± VAR_CUTOFF ± VAR_RATE_HONOUR ± VAR_FX_TIMING) + reseller earnings (RESELL_REVENUE − RESELL_COST), each callable on its own and together, by project, partner, pair or month, per currency; one figure across currencies is a REPORTING_VALUE (v5.7, D46).

Notes

  • Every deal belongs to a deal group. DEAL_GROUP is the client-facing instruction: the pair as the sender sees it, the sender rate, fee, reference and entry mode. A plain single-partner deal is a group of one leg; a route that needs two partners (INR → USDT at Ali, USDT → EUR at Jeton) has two forward legs; a rejected payout is unwound with a return leg.
  • Legs. leg_type forward or return; funding_source collection, prior_leg (leg 2 of a route, no collection) or returned_settlement (a return leg). Priced once and partner fixed at quote hold per leg. Attribution is to the receiver group: set at quote on the first forward leg, inherited by leg n of a route from leg n−1 and by a return leg from its parent leg. The receiver is optional until settlement.
  • Two entry modes as before: collect-first legs are born in state Collected with priced_at = conversion time; quote-first legs carry sent / valid / grace timestamps and a late decision. An estimate-first mode gives an indicative figure and prices at conversion.
  • Conversion has exactly one owner: a deal leg or a BALANCE_CONVERSION. The receiver-side fee is taken at conversion. Amounts are rounded at conversion by the pair's option (D25); a dropped fraction (rounding_residual, signed) stays client money in the balance and pays out when it reaches a unit, an amount added by rounding up is NPL's cost. NPL's margin is captured at conversion and is never again at risk from a return or a forward.
  • Balance conversion is NPL converting a client's held balance (5K SGD → USDT to fund a 15K USDT payout): Finance-initiated, Management-approved, no sender, receiver or collection, same rate machinery, markup by FEE_DECISION. It names the receiver group it serves; ENTITLEMENT_REATTRIBUTION moves that group's entitlement to the new currency, and any excess over the group's entitlement is booked as an approved offset.
  • Reroute is the only way partner or partner entity change after quote. Forwarding is forward_full or forward_and_recover_dues: NPL nets what the alternate partner owes it (EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE) against the funds forwarded, within the outstanding receivable, with the partner's agreement recorded. Post-collection outcome is via the own wallet or a refund to the sender.
  • One settlement model: SETTLEMENT drains one partner's holding into one or many SETTLEMENT_LINEs, rounded as the pair says. Under settlement_policy to_zero the balance after release is less than one unit; under hold_allowed the balance may rest at the partner within the project's exposure cap.
  • A line paying a counterparty receiver whose group differs from the paying leg's attributed group is an offset, created by the same action, with Management approval and tighter aging. A line paying a sender_return or partner_transit receiver is never an offset: those receivers have no group, and the line debits the group of the leg it names in deal_id (D13, D17).
  • Rejected payout. When the receiving or intermediary bank rejects a transfer, SETTLEMENT_RETURN records the returned amount, bank fee and reason; the line's outcome becomes returned, a reversing ledger transaction puts the money back into the client's balance and the paying leg's group entitlement, and BANK_FEE_EVENT books the bounce fee. The money then stays in balance for later payouts, or funds a return leg — attributed to the same group — that converts back and pays the sender's return receiver.
  • Fee decisions. FEE_DECISION is a one-off, approved decision on a single subject: markup applied or waived on a return leg or balance conversion, a network-fee override on a refund, a bank-fee treatment override on one settlement. Standing rules stay in FEE_STRUCTURE and FEE_OVERRIDE.
  • CONFIRMATION is full or short; a short confirmation opens a SHORTFALL topped up by a later settlement or an explicit separate payout — cash found short at hand-over included. Rounding differences no longer land here. MARKUP_SHARE_ACCRUAL and PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL accrue per deal under their rules; a party_retains markup-share accrual is a receivable from the party, reconciled monthly like a rebate (D26); rebates are reconciled monthly against the partner's statement, which covers NPLify deals only (D27).
  • Pricing stamps (v5.3). A leg stamps the override and the base tier that priced it; a leg that crosses a tier threshold holds two DEAL_FEE_TIER portions and a blended fee (D20, D21). The deal group stamps the customer-facing fee and rate the quote printed (D22). On a pair that needs a bank lock the leg records rate_locked_at and conversion_due_date: locked before the partner's cutoff it converts the same day, otherwise the next business day at that day's version; the sender's figures are write-once, NPL absorbs the difference as a cutoff-timing variance, and a conversion whose next-day rate breaches the margin is deferred with a reason. The client balance view shows the locked leg's converted value as pending from the lock; a void removes it (D29). QUOTE_PACKAGE is the record of what was sent for a deal group — template version, channel, printed figures, sent_at, hash — one row per issue; a quote-first leg is Sent only when a package has sent_at, re-issues are new rows, a new price is a new deal group (D35).
  • Invoices. INVOICE is an obligation in its own currency — a vendor's EUR invoice a reseller customer pays in THB or USDT, in parts, over days. A deal group names the invoice it pays (advance, then balance); each payout line records how much of the obligation it discharged and the market snapshot used; INVOICE_BALANCE is the open remainder (D24).
  • Cash and crypto parts. A cash part carries the token (the local-currency bill whose serial identifies the agent), the agent's contact and the partner's count; the leg carries the city, which also selects the rate version (D30). A crypto part carries the sender's declared address and the screening that admitted it, unless the project skips up-front screening (D31).
  • Loss events. LOSS_EVENT records money lost after it was verified or released — a frozen local account, cash short that cannot be recovered, a wrong-chain transfer — on either side, by any method, for a partial or full amount, with the loss split across sender, NPL, partner and client; Management approves the split, one reversing transaction posts it, and a collection-side event moves the part to reversed (D32).

4 · Ledger & controls domain

Diagram 4. OWN_WALLET, RECEIVER, SENDER, MARKUP_SHARE_PARTY are defined in Diagram 1a; PARTNER_CONFIG in 1b; COLLECTION, INVOICE in 3a; CONVERSION, BALANCE_CONVERSION, REROUTE, EARNINGS_OFFSET in 3b; SETTLEMENT, SETTLEMENT_RETURN, CONFIRMATION, BANK_FEE_EVENT, MARKUP_SHARE_ACCRUAL, PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL, LOSS_EVENT, LOSS_RECOVERY in 3c.

Notes

  • Client due balances are held as one account per project × partner × currency (CL.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.DUE); group entitlement is a view, not an account. holder_type never includes a settlement rail or narrative entity.
  • Ownership flips client → company at one event only: margin recognition at conversion. NPL never advances money to a receiver, and withholding on a reroute is not a separate event because the margin is always captured by whichever partner converts.
  • Recover dues on a reroute posts own-wallet cash against the earnings receivable at the partner: company money on both sides, no income.
  • Transaction sources: Collection, Conversion, BalanceConversion, Settlement, SettlementReturn, Confirmation, BankFeeEvent, Reroute, MarkupShare, Rebate, LossEvent, Adjustment. Account purposes include PAYABLE, SHARE_PAYABLE, SHARE_RECEIVABLE, REBATE_RECEIVABLE, EARN_GROSS, EARN_REBATE, EXP_ROUNDING and EXP_LOSS; ADVANCE does not exist. Cost components include share, rebate, rounding, fx_timing, cutoff_timing and loss.
  • Three streams NPL never mixes (v5.3). Earnings on deals post to EARN_GROSS at conversion; a partner's rebate posts to EARN_REBATE and is never in the base a client party shares (D26, D27); NPL's remainder from a party that holds the converted funds sits in SHARE_RECEIVABLE until the party pays it. The cost of rounding up is EXP_ROUNDING, NPL's share of a loss event is EXP_LOSS; the client's and sender's shares of a loss reduce the client balance, the partner's share is a receivable from the partner (D25, D32). Own-desk deals use the ordinary partner-coded accounts with the own-desk configuration as holder and EXP_PARTNER zero by construction (D23).
  • One system-settings area (D43, D44): SYSTEM_SETTING holds NPL-wide, Management-approved keys — the reporting currency, its staleness limit, the operating time zone; ROLE holds the user roles and ROLE_RIGHT what each may initiate and approve per controlled action, with the role added on escalation; platform-scope CURRENCY_PAIRs carry the conversion rates through the ordinary rate-source chain. REPORTING_VALUE converts any per-currency figure into the reporting currency at the latest market rate of its platform pair, as a display-only estimate that carries the rate it used (D43). APPROVAL, AUDIT_LOG and RECORD_LOCK are modelled once and apply to all master data. Approver ≠ initiator on every approval; Operations never sees derived economics. Approval actions include refund_to_third_party, cross_group_payout, balance_conversion, recover_dues, enable_own_desk, approve_loss_split and override_screening_reject. cross_group_payout never fires on a line paying a sender_return or partner_transit receiver. Wallet screening itself is an Operations action, not an approval (D31).

5 · Invariants (enforced at write time)

  1. Postings in one transaction sum to zero per currency.
  2. Ledger tables are append-only; corrections are reversing transactions.
  3. Custody in NPL’s own wallet is allowed in three cases only: a collection on a deal with an approved REROUTE; a leg whose PARTNER_CONFIG is an own desk (D23, the NPL-GR project); or a collection on a wallet with role collection_bridge, which is forwarded to the leg’s partner as a hop (a SETTLEMENT_LINE to the partner_transit receiver) within the wallet’s custody_max_hours (D40). CL.OWN.*.HELD is debited by nothing else; the custody aging view reports all three and is the standing control.
  4. Settle to the residual: under settlement_policy = to_zero a SETTLEMENT pays the balance rounded by the pair’s option and leaves only the rounding residual (dust stays client money; a round-up is NPL’s cost — D25); under hold_allowed the balance may rest at the partner within the project’s exposure cap (Q5, Q8).
  5. Priced once, per leg: a leg’s pricing fields are write-once after priced_at; a re-quote is a new leg or a new deal group.
  6. Partner fixed at quote, per leg: partner_pair_id / partner_entity_id change only through an approved REROUTE. A collection’s endpoint must belong to the leg’s partner entity (v5.1, D15). Its kind must match the leg’s collection_method — wallet for crypto, bank for bank, no endpoint for cash (v5.2, D19). A COLLECTION may reference only an active endpoint; a bank endpoint is active only with rail set (D18).
  7. Entitlement conservation: Σ GROUP_ENTITLEMENT over a project’s groups = Σ PROJECT_BALANCE over partners, per currency, including balance-conversion re-attributions. Return and hop legs preserve this because they inherit the parent leg’s group (D13). Since v5.2 every payout line resolves to a group — the paid receiver’s for a counterparty, the paying leg’s via deal_id otherwise — so this is checkable mechanically (D17).
  8. Destination approval precedes collection: a quote-first deal cannot leave Inquiry unless at least one account in the entitled group has a DESTINATION_APPROVAL in state approved with the chosen partner.
  9. Approver ≠ initiator on every APPROVAL, and the approver’s ROLE has may_approve for the action in ROLE_RIGHT while the initiator’s has may_initiate; Operations never receives derived-economics fields (ROLE.sees_economics) (restated v5.4, D44).
  10. Every balance shown anywhere is a sum over postings or deals.
  11. A collect-first deal requires an existing SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW entry for its sender and group (Q1).
  12. A return leg pays the sender_return RECEIVER linked to the parent leg’s sender, unless a Management-approved exception with a reason names another approved receiver.
  13. The failed forward line is reversed before a return leg opens, so entitlement and balance are correct at the return conversion.
  14. A CONVERSION belongs to exactly one owner: a deal leg or a balance conversion.
  15. A recovery on a reroute cannot exceed the outstanding EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE at that partner; the alternate partner’s expected conversion is computed on the net amount forwarded.
  16. Ownership moves between client and company at four events only: margin recognition at conversion (client → company); an EARNINGS_OFFSET (company → client at one partner and client → company at another, the same value at the partner’s rate of the day); the forex true-up of a line that discharges an invoice obligation (either way); and the partial reversal of a loss make-good when a Management-approved share is borne by the client. NPL never advances money to a receiver (Q13). Every transaction balances per owner as well as per currency (restated v5.7, D46).
  17. Offsets arise only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to a different group, and carry Management approval and tighter aging. A project with one group never has an offset; within a group nothing is tracked beyond an informational tally (v5.0).
  18. A RECEIVER has a group_id if and only if kind = counterparty. Forward legs and the sender allow list target counterparty groups and receivers only. A return leg inherits receiver_group_id from its parent leg; leg n of a route inherits it from leg n−1 (v5.0, D13).
  19. A SETTLEMENT_LINE paying a group-less receiver (sender_return, partner_transit) carries deal_id; the paying leg’s group is a stored fact, never inferred (v5.2, D17).
  20. A FEE_OVERRIDE with its own split has both share columns set and they sum to its pct; with neither set the structure’s proportion applies. The leg stamps the override that priced it (v5.3, D20).
  21. The base tier stamped on a leg is the tier with the highest min_monthly_volume not exceeding the project’s calendar-month volume at quote (PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME); a leg that takes the month past a threshold is split into two DEAL_FEE_TIER portions whose amounts sum to amount_in, and its fee parts are the blended sum (v5.3, D21).
  22. Customer-facing figures are derived, never typed: customer_facing_rate = sender_rate ÷ (1 − customer_facing_fee_pct), stamped at quote; the true rates and fee parts are stored beside them and Operations sees the customer-facing pair only (v5.3, D22).
  23. Σ obligation_discharged over an invoice’s confirmed lines never exceeds its amount; a line that names an invoice names a deal_id whose deal group is on that invoice (v5.3, D24).
  24. Rounding is the pair’s configured option — amount_rounding / rounding_unit on payouts, cash_rounding / cash_rounding_unit on the cash amount collected; the residual is signed — a dropped fraction stays client money in the balance, an amount added by rounding up is NPL’s cost posted to EXP_ROUNDING — so every rounding difference has an owner (v5.3, D25).
  25. Σ pct of the share_of_net_markup rules active on one leg ≤ 100 %; the share base is the leg’s fee parts less its partner cost and never includes a partner rebate. A MARKUP_SHARE_ACCRUAL is created and posted by the conversion it arises on; a party_retains accrual is a receivable from the party, reconciled monthly (v5.3, D26; restated v5.7, D46).
  26. Rebate income posts only to EARN_REBATE, never to EARN_GROSS; every rebate accrual names the NPLify deal it arises on, is created and posted by that deal’s conversion in the rule’s payout currency, and the partner statement is reconciled against those deals alone (v5.3, D27; restated v5.7, D46).
  27. A partner rate version stores the rate as quoted and its direction; the normalised rate is derived (1 ÷ quoted when the directions differ, at the pair’s precision) and is subject to the breach check like any other, so a direction slip freezes the pair instead of pricing a deal (v5.3, D28).
  28. The partner’s cutoff binds two events on pairs that rely on the banking channel. The effective cutoff for a day is the one-day PARTNER_CUTOFF_OVERRIDE if any, else the weekday rule, else PARTNER.bank_cutoff_time, and is stamped (cutoff_at) on the leg at rate lock and on the settlement at approval. A leg’s conversion_due_date is the lock date when rate_locked_at precedes cutoff_at and the next business day otherwise, and Converting may not start before it; a bank-rail settlement’s execution_due_date follows the same rule from its approval time. The sender’s figures are write-once (invariant 5); the difference between the stamped partner rate and the rate actually used posts to VAR_CUTOFF with component cutoff_timing — NPL absorbs it (v5.3, D29, amended 9 October).
  29. A rate version is unique per partner × pair × day × location; a cash leg carries its cash_location and prices on a version of that location; a cash part is verified only after the partner’s count (counted_at) (v5.3, D30).
  30. A crypto collection names its sending address and, unless the project skips up-front screening, the screening that admitted it; a screening decided accept_alternate may land only on an endpoint whose risk_band is elevated, and no collection exists for a decision of reject unless Finance overrides it (v5.3, D31).
  31. A single_use endpoint or account is referenced by at most one collection or payout line, for the deal it was reserved for, and retires when that reference is verified or confirmed. A LOSS_EVENT’s shares sum to its amount, which never exceeds the amount verified or released; a collection-side event moves the part to reversed and the client balance never goes below zero (v5.3, D32).
  32. A pair whose two currencies are the same is converted at rate 1 like any other pair, so the sender and receiver fee parts are captured at conversion and the balance arithmetic is unchanged (v5.3, D33).
  33. Business days are computed, never assumed: ‘next business day’ for a conversion due date or a settlement execution date skips weekends in the partner’s cutoff_timezone and the partner’s HOLIDAY rows of the matching scope; a reroute with trigger holiday names a day that is a HOLIDAY of scope partner (v5.3, D34).
  34. A quote-first leg leaves Quoted for Sent only when a QUOTE_PACKAGE of its group has sent_at; the package’s content_hash is the leg’s quote_hash and its printed figures equal the group’s customer-facing figures (derived, never typed); freshness runs from the leg’s market snapshot (MARKET_RATE.captured_at) to sent_at within PROJECT.quote_freshness_min, validity from sent_at. Packages are append-only: a re-issue supersedes, a new price is a new deal group. A quote template prints sender-facing fields only (v5.3, D35, D36).
  35. Client-level figures are sums over the client’s projects, never stored (CLIENT_POSITION); when CLIENT.exposure_ceiling is set, Σ PROJECT_BALANCE across the client’s projects may not exceed it — a settlement or a held balance that would breach it needs Management approval, as a project’s own ceiling does (v5.4, D38).
  36. A partner offers only what its record says: a leg’s collection_method, and the method of any settlement through the partner, must be in PARTNER.supported_methods; a wallet endpoint’s network must already exist as an endpoint of that partner’s vehicle before a collection may name it. Adding a method or a network is a Management-approved configuration change (v5.4, D39).
  37. A quote’s validity may be extended any number of times before the validity in force ends, each time by an APPROVAL (extend_quote_validity) recorded as a QUOTE_VALIDITY_EXTENSION that moves effective_valid_until and re-issues the quote package at the same price; Finance approves, Management is added when the new validity passes the partner’s cutoff or the rate version’s expiry. The pricing fields stay write-once (invariant 5). After the validity in force ends, the paths are the grace decision and a new deal group (v5.5, D45; was once-only within grace, D42).
  38. Converted figures are display-only estimates: a REPORTING_VALUE is computed at read time from the latest MARKET_RATE of the platform CURRENCY_PAIR (priced through its PAIR_RATE_SOURCE chain), carries the rate and its time, is flagged when the rate is older than reporting_rate_max_age_min, and is never posted, stored, quoted or settled. The only controls that read it are ceilings stated in the reporting currency (CLIENT.exposure_ceiling); every other limit and every posting stays in its own currency (v5.4, D43).
  39. An expired quote is never revived: the sender gets a new deal group. At the sender’s request that new leg may be priced on the earlier leg’s market rate and partner rate version (rate_reused_from_deal_id) by an approved override (honour_expired_rate, Finance), the automated rate set aside and the grace drift limit not applied; the leg stamps the reused rates as its own, and the difference against the partner’s actual rate at conversion posts to VAR_RATE_HONOUR — NPL’s cost, chosen (v5.5, D45).
  40. A settlement discharges CL.PROJECT.<CCY>.PAYABLE when the partner releases the money (released_at); a SETTLEMENT_RETURN re-raises it for what came back and a short CONFIRMATION for the part not delivered; a full confirmation posts nothing; a hop (partner_transit) posts only when the far side credits and never touches the promise. Every released line ends confirmed, short or returned, and ‘sent, not yet confirmed’ is read from the line, never from an account (v5.7, D46).
  41. CO.<PARTNER>.<CCY>.POOL may be below zero only between a fee NPL absorbed in a currency where it held nothing at that partner and the next conversion there, which then includes NPL’s own USDT converted alongside the client’s (a Conversion with a company part through FX_CLEARING); Finance squares every negative pool within the month (v5.7, D46).
  42. Fee parts are percentages of the principal at the basis rate and never compound: fee_sender_part = amount_in × rate × sender_pays_pct, fee_receiver_part = amount_in × rate × receiver_pays_pct, client_net = amount_in × rate × (1 − sender_pays_pct − receiver_pays_pct) (v5.7, D46).
  43. An EARNINGS_OFFSET is neutral for the client: from_amount at the from-partner becomes the client’s and to_amount = from_amount ÷ the to-partner’s rate of the day becomes NPL’s, with the client’s promises re-denominated by the same amounts; to_amount never exceeds the client’s unconverted balance at the to-partner, from_amount never exceeds NPL’s pool at the from-partner, and the receivables it recovers are marked recovered_by_offset_id (v5.7, D46).
  44. In NPL-GR the vendor and resale invoices are posted once each, in the invoice currency (RESELL_COST / VENDOR_PAYABLE; RESALE_RECEIVABLE / RESELL_REVENUE), and no later transaction touches RESELL_REVENUE or RESELL_COST: the reseller revenue is intact by construction. The customer’s payment clears RESALE_RECEIVABLE into REMIT_CLAIM; each discharging line clears VENDOR_PAYABLE or REMIT_CLAIM; the forex result of instalments posts to VAR_FX_TIMING on the remittance side (v5.7, D46).

6 · What changed from v4.0

Draft v5.7 (11 October 2026) is v5.6 plus D46, the ledger design agreed with NPL on 10–11 October: two new tables (EARNINGS_OFFSET, LOSS_RECOVERY), three new views (RESELLER_MARGIN, REMITTANCE_MARGIN, NPL_PROFIT), the ledger vocabulary of the Ledger Posting Design v5.7, and invariants 40–44. Draft v5.6 (9 October 2026) was v5.5 with the examples anonymised; v5.5 closed the 8–9 October work: v5.4 added the CLIENT parent (D38) and, through the evening, D39–D44. v5.3 applied the thirteen fee-practice gaps found between NPL's fee table, NPL’s workbook answers and the Project Context / Payment methods tabs and ERD v5.2 — written up as proposals A–M in "Model Gaps & Proposals v1.0" and confirmed by NPL on 8–9 October — plus the same-currency rule, as decisions D20–D33. Fourteen tables are added (CLIENT, SYSTEM_SETTING, ROLE, ROLE_RIGHT, QUOTE_VALIDITY_EXTENSION, FEE_TIER, DEAL_FEE_TIER, INVOICE, WALLET_SCREENING, LOSS_EVENT, PARTNER_CUTOFF_OVERRIDE, HOLIDAY, QUOTE_PACKAGE, MESSAGE_TEMPLATE) and five views (INVOICE_BALANCE, PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME, CLIENT_POSITION, WALLET_REGISTRY, REPORTING_VALUE): 70 tables and 12 views. Earlier: v5.0 / v5.1 (7 October) removed the return group (D13), gave accounts explicit wallet fields (D14) and restructured the partner's collection side (D15); v5.2 (8 October 2026) added D16–D19.

v5.3 to v5.7 — the fee-practice decisions, the FRS-term additions, the naming alignment, the client parent, NPL's operational answers and the ledger design (11 October 2026)

D46 — The ledger design: variance by cause, loss first, accruals at conversion, the reseller books, earnings kept unconverted and offset, sent is discharged

Decision. Eight parts, from the Ledger Posting Design v5.7 and NPL's answers of 10–11 October. (1) LEDGER_ACCOUNT.purpose VARIANCE becomes VAR_CONVERSION, VAR_CUTOFF, VAR_RATE_HONOUR and VAR_FX_TIMING. (2) A LOSS_EVENT is booked to NPL in full and the client made whole in one transaction (EXP_LOSS; MAKEGOOD / LOSS_PAYABLE when it cannot be funded at once); each share is then a LOSS_RECOVERY posting; a partial loss posts the lost part only. (3) Markup-share and rebate accruals are created and posted by the conversion; PARTNER_REBATE_RULE.payout_currency. (4) NPL-GR keeps two invoices per deal in EUR — INVOICE.kind vendor / resale, sender_id — posted once as cost and revenue (source Invoice, component resale), so the reseller revenue is intact by construction (RESELLER_MARGIN); the remittance deal that collects the resale invoice posts like any client project with NPL-GR as the client, the THB collected as cash and rounded, and each instalment's forex result is a true-up to VAR_FX_TIMING (REMITTANCE_MARGIN); NPL_PROFIT = remittance + reseller earnings, each callable alone. (5) Earnings may be kept in the unconverted balance (CONVERSION.residual_in) and offset between partners (EARNINGS_OFFSET at the to-partner's rate of the day, recovering EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE rows; Finance requests, Management approves), recorded for NPL in FX_CLEARING. (6) FX_CLEARING for any company balance settled in another currency. (7) The promise is discharged on release: INTRANSIT retired, a return or a short confirmation re-raises PAYABLE, a full confirmation posts nothing, a hop posts on credit; CURRENCY_PAIR.amount_rounding gains exact (bank transfers carry cents, unit rounding is for cash); a pool may be negative only until the next conversion squares it with NPL's own USDT. (8) Fee parts are percentages of the principal at the basis rate, never compounded; network fees in USDT, absent when none applies. Invariants 16, 25, 26, 28, 39 restated; 40–44 new.

Rejected alternative. A single VARIANCE account; the reseller books as invoice records with views only; the market rate for an offset; INTRANSIT as a client asset; recognising the vendor invoice as cost when discharged rather than when received.

Why. NPL (10–11 October): the ledger must show where NPL's margin physically is (it is taken out of unconverted collections and offset between partners), prove the reseller revenue untouched whatever the remittance side does, answer ‘NPL's profit’ with both businesses, and treat sent money as out of NPL's hands. Fee facts folded in: Evo USDT → EUR sender 1 % or 1.4 % with receiver 0.6 %, EUR → EUR 2.8 % split 50/50, Jeton 1.25 %, Ali assumed 1 % inside its rate, NPL-GR THB collected as cash.

D20 (A) — A per-sender override carries its own split

Decision. FEE_OVERRIDE gains sender_pays_pct and receiver_pays_pct; both blank means the structure's proportion, both set means they sum to pct. DEAL stamps fee_override_id.

Rejected alternative. Keeping the override as a total only, with the structure's proportion.

Why. Evo's selected senders pay 1.0 % while Evo still pays its 0.6 %; a proportional override would charge 1.12 % and 0.48 %. NPL confirmed the receiver part is fixed for every sender.

D21 (B) — Fees by monthly volume

Decision. FEE_TIER under a fee structure (one tier at volume 0); the tier is chosen at quote from the project's calendar-month volume (PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME) and stamped with the volume that justified it. A leg that takes the month past a threshold is split: DEAL_FEE_TIER holds the portion below the threshold at the lower tier and the portion above at the next, and the leg's fee parts are the blended sum.

Rejected alternative. A rolling 30-day window; switching the whole leg to the new tier; switching from the next leg only.

Why. GDC pays 2.5 % below USD 500,000 a month and 2.25 % above, switched by hand today. NPL: calendar month; the crossing transaction itself attributes the part above the threshold to the lower tier.

D22 (C) — What the quote prints

Decision. FEE_STRUCTURE.customer_facing_fee_basis (actual / sender_pays_on_agent_rate / fixed) and customer_facing_fee_pct; DEAL_GROUP stamps customer_facing_fee_pct and customer_facing_rate = sender_rate ÷ (1 − customer-facing fee) so a re-printed quote matches. Customer-facing figures are derived, never typed; Operations sees the customer-facing pair, Finance both.

Rejected alternative. Leaving the recomputation of the 'market rate' to Operations by hand.

Why. BF quotes via Ali show 'fee 1 %' while the recorded parts add to 1.4 % (Ali's 1 % inside its rate plus NPL's 0.4 %). NPL: a BF-only rule, to be cleared when the project moves to partner rate plus markup. The Raeen sub-account quote uses the same recomputation.

D23 (D) — NPL-GR as an own-desk project

Decision. PARTNER_CONFIG.is_own_desk; an own wallet is a COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT under it (own_wallet_id); own-desk pairs are priced market plus NPL's markup with generated rate versions; invariant 3 restated: client money may rest in NPL's wallet under an approved reroute or in an own-desk project, and the custody view reports both. Enabling an own desk is a Management-approved configuration change (enable_own_desk).

Rejected alternative. Keeping the no-custody principle intact and running the game-reseller flows outside NPLify.

Why. The reseller products (Bala, Fair, 66 Group, TripleSeven, Alpha Plus, 27 Group via THB cash) collect into NPL's own wallet and pay vendors from it on later days; there is no outside partner for the conversion. NPL's framing: NPL-GR, a business unit of NPL, is the client. Management confirmed running it inside the system.

D24 (E) — Invoices paid in parts

Decision. INVOICE owned by the project, naming the vendor; DEAL_GROUP.invoice_id; SETTLEMENT_LINE gains invoice_id, obligation_discharged, discharge_rate and the market snapshot used; INVOICE_BALANCE = amount − Σ discharged over confirmed lines. The EUR difference between what was collected and what was discharged posts to variance with component fx_timing.

Rejected alternative. Tracking the obligation in a free-text client reference.

Why. A vendor's EUR invoice is settled in USDT in instalments at different days' rates (EUR/USDT 0.8708 at collection, 0.87527 at the last payment); the open balance changes with every instalment. NPL: wanted; vendors are paid on different days and the forex difference is accepted within the 2 % markup.

D25 (F) — A rounding menu per pair

Decision. CURRENCY_PAIR.amount_rounding grows from one value to truncate_unit / nearest_unit / round_up_unit / nearest_n / round_up_n with rounding_unit; CONVERSION.rounding_residual is signed — a dropped fraction stays client money, an amount added by rounding up is NPL's cost in EXP_ROUNDING. Cash collections use the same menu on the collected amount (cash_rounding with cash_rounding_unit).

Rejected alternative. Truncation only, with the other practices left outside the system.

Why. Live quotes round THB and INR to the nearest 1,000 and round a reseller customer's USDT up. NPL: round up to the nearest 1,000 for Asian currencies, nearest unit for USD, SGD, HKD; round-up on USDT is deliberate.

D26 (G) — Markup shared with a client party

Decision. MARKUP_SHARE_RULE basis share_of_net_markup: the base is the leg's fee parts less its partner cost, on amount × market, rebates never included; party_kind markup-share party / client_party; settlement_mode npl_pays / party_retains; optional scope by fee structure; several rules per project with Σ shares ≤ 100 %. MARKUP_SHARE_ACCRUAL gains direction, period and received_amount; a party_retains accrual is a receivable (SHARE_RECEIVABLE) reconciled monthly.

Rejected alternative. A fixed percentage per party, reconfigured when the route changes; NPL always paying the share out.

Why. Raeen's downlines fund sub-accounts at 4 %; whatever is left after the partner's fee is split equally — 1.5 % each via Ali, 1.6 % each via Aquanow — Raeen keeps the converted EUR in its own Aquanow account and pays NPL monthly; direct downlines split 0.2 % 75 / 25. NPL: future deals may have several parties with different shares; the partner's rebate is NPL's alone and not visible to the party.

D27 (H) — Rebates as their own stream

Decision. Rebate income posts to EARN_REBATE, never EARN_GROSS. PARTNER_REBATE_RULE gains basis (pct_of_amount / pct_of_partner_fee) and pct, retires the old pct_of_partner_fee column (amended 9 October), and gains an optional scope by sender or fee structure. PARTNER_REBATE_ACCRUAL keeps deal_id required and gains statement_ref.

Rejected alternative. Accruals without a deal for clients NPL referred but does not service.

Why. NPL: the partner statement that NPLify reconciles covers only deals NPLify handled — customers working with Jeton or Aquanow directly are out of scope. Jeton pays 0.4 % of the amount on a 1 % or 1.25 % fee and 0.3 % on Novi's 0.9 %, so the rebate is not a fixed share of the fee. Management reads earnings and rebates as two numbers.

D28 (I) — Partner rates as quoted

Decision. PARTNER_RATE_VERSION gains quoted_rate and quoted_direction; rate is derived (1 ÷ quoted when the directions differ, at the pair's precision) and goes through the breach check like any rate.

Rejected alternative. A single normalised rate typed by Operations.

Why. Ali sometimes states USDT → EUR as 1.1738 (EUR-per-USDT the other way round); the hand inversion is a 38 % error waiting to happen, and the audit trail should show the number the partner sent.

D29 (J) — Bank cutoff, rate lock, next-day conversion

Decision. PARTNER.bank_cutoff_time / cutoff_timezone (amended 9 October: on PARTNER, not PARTNER_CONFIG — the cutoff is the partner's, whichever project uses it), with PARTNER_CUTOFF_OVERRIDE for a one-day extension the partner agreed (30–60 minutes, urgent requests) or an early close (Fridays, pre-holiday); PARTNER_PAIR.needs_bank_lock for the pairs that rely on the banking channel; the effective cutoff is stamped as cutoff_at on the leg at rate lock and on the settlement at approval, and SETTLEMENT.execution_due_date applies the same rule to the outgoing bank transfer — the second event the cutoff governs; DEAL and BALANCE_CONVERSION carry rate_locked_at and conversion_due_date (the lock date before the cutoff, else the next business day; Converting may not start earlier) and a conversion_deferred_reason. The client balance view shows a locked leg's converted value as pending from the lock; a void removes it. The difference between the stamped partner rate and the one used posts to variance with component cutoff_timing.

Rejected alternative. Treating the cutoff as part of quote validity; re-quoting the sender the next day.

Why. Evo via Ali: the rate is compared in the morning; locked before 14:30 GMT+8 it converts the same day, otherwise the money is collected on the morning's figures and converted the next business day. AK's USD and SGD balances are banking-ready and wait too. NPL: NPL absorbs the difference; if Ali's next-day rate breaches the margin, ask for a better rate or wait a day; today's balances should show the pending converted value.

D30 (K) — Cash by token, rates per city

Decision. DEAL.cash_location; PARTNER_RATE_VERSION.location with uniqueness per partner × pair × day × location; COLLECTION gains token_ref, agent_contact_ref and counted_at, with cash states token_issued → handed_over → counted → verified; SETTLEMENT_LINE.token_ref for cash payouts.

Rejected alternative. Free-text cash instructions on the deal and one rate per currency; making the city a side of the currency pair (CASH_LOCATION) — proposed and withdrawn on 9 October at NPL's request.

Why. A cash collection or settlement is arranged by token — a local-currency bill whose serial number identifies the agent — closed by a photo of the token and the partner's count; INR in Delhi and Mumbai, or USD cash in Bangkok and Singapore, are different agents at different rates.

D31 (L) — Wallet screening

Decision. WALLET_SCREENING per address and day for sending and receiving wallets (result, decision, who, when, evidence); COLLECTION gains sending_address, wallet_screening_id and screening_skipped; COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT.risk_band; DESTINATION_APPROVAL.wallet_screening_id. A screening decided accept_alternate lands only on an elevated-band endpoint; a reject is overridden only by Finance.

Rejected alternative. A static risk tier on the sender.

Why. NPL screens the sender's declared wallet before giving out the partner's receiving wallet, routes elevated-risk wallets to alternate wallets, verifies the hash on chain, and screens receivers' wallets before settlement. NPL: screening is a transaction-coordination activity, so it is an Operations action and Operations sees the result. Not every Evo sender accepts up-front screening.

D32 (M) — Single-use accounts and loss events

Decision. COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT and RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT gain usage single_use with reserved_for_deal_id (and an expected amount on the endpoint); LOSS_EVENT on either side, by any method, for a partial or full amount, with the loss split across sender, NPL, partner and client (shares sum to the amount, Management approves); one reversing transaction (source LossEvent); EXP_LOSS; COLLECTION.state reversed. Cash found short at hand-over is a short confirmation topped up at the next settlement or by a separate payout, and a loss event only when unrecoverable.

Rejected alternative. A collection-only reversal borne by the sender in full.

Why. Local deposits use accounts the partner lends for one transaction; a frozen account can lose the funds. NPL: the loss can be partial, can be shared between NPL and the partner as well as the sender, can happen on the settlement side and by other methods, and single-use local accounts are used for settlement too.

D34 — Holiday calendar as dates

Decision. HOLIDAY under PARTNER: one row per non-business day of the partner's banking channel, with a scope (bank channel only, or the partner altogether) and a source. PARTNER.holiday_calendar becomes the name of the source calendar. Every "next business day" in the model — a leg's conversion_due_date, a settlement's execution_due_date — skips weekends in the partner's time zone and these rows; a reroute triggered by a holiday names one.

Rejected alternative. Keeping the calendar as a text label on PARTNER (the v4.0 shape).

Why. Since D29 the model computes due dates across the cutoff, and a label cannot be counted from. The FRS names the holiday calendar as a thing the system holds.

D35 — The quote package as a record

Decision. QUOTE_PACKAGE under DEAL_GROUP: one row per issue — the template version that rendered it, the channel, the rendered document reference, the printed sender-facing figures, sent_at, sent_by and a content_hash. The leg's quote_hash and sent_at are the package's. A re-issue (wording, another channel) is a new row that supersedes the earlier one; a new price is a new deal group. A quote-first leg is Sent only when a package has sent_at; freshness runs from the leg's market snapshot to sent_at, validity from sent_at.

Rejected alternative. Keeping only the facts behind the quote (rates, fees, timestamps, a hash) and not the artefact sent.

Why. Priced-once and the quote clocks rest on what the sender was actually shown; in a dispute the stored facts are not the document. The FRS's quote package had no home.

D36 — Message templates

Decision. MESSAGE_TEMPLATE: versioned wording of outgoing messages (quote, payment instructions, confirmation request, settlement advice, cash token), global or owned by a project, on a channel and in a language, with printed_fields — the model fields it may print. A quote template prints sender-facing figures only (sender rate, customer-facing fee and rate, amount out, validity), never partner rates, margins or costs. Management approves template changes as configuration.

Rejected alternative. Templates kept in the application layer with no record in the model.

Why. A quote package has to name what rendered it, and the rule that Operations never passes derived economics to a sender (invariant 9) is enforceable only if the template declares what it prints.

D38 — A CLIENT above PROJECT

Decision. CLIENT: the commercial relationship NPL contracts with and reports on — name, category (NPL's own grouping from the Project Context tab), legal entity and KYC references, relationship owner, status, and an optional exposure_ceiling on the sum resting at partners across its projects. PROJECT gains client_id: a project is one arrangement with a client. CLIENT_POSITION rolls up balances, entitlement, custody, earnings and rebates over the client's projects — a view, never stored (invariant 35). The per-project view CLIENT_BALANCE is renamed PROJECT_BALANCE so the two cannot be confused. Parties stay per project.

Rejected alternative. Keeping project = client and reporting across projects by hand; or moving senders, receivers and accounts up to the client now.

Why. NPL: one client runs several complex arrangements (BF, BF Sub and BF Withdrawal are one client; 66 Group appears in remittance and in the game reseller), so with project = client there was no way to report per client. Moving the party tables up would change attribution, the allow list and registrations, which is the kind of change that is expensive after launch; a client-wide sender registry can be added later as a reference.

D39 — A partner's methods are configuration

Decision. PARTNER gains supported_methods (crypto / bank / cash / local_deposit) and its bank_cutoff_time becomes nullable — empty for Jeton and Aquanow, which bind nothing. Invariant 36: a leg's collection method and a settlement's method must be among the partner's methods, and a wallet endpoint's network must already exist under the partner's vehicle before a collection may name it; adding either is a Management-approved configuration change. Networks are not declared: the vehicle's wallet endpoints already say them.

Rejected alternative. Deriving everything from the configured endpoints and rails.

Why. Cash and local deposits have no standing endpoint (D19, D32), so whether a partner offers them cannot be read from the configuration until a deal is attempted. NPL: Jeton has no cash or local methods and no cutoff; a partner record must be customizable, not hard-coded.

D40 — Bridge wallets and the wallet registry

Decision. OWN_WALLET gains role (reroute_contingency / own_desk / collection_bridge) and networks. Invariant 3 is restated with a third allowed case: a collection on a bridge wallet, forwarded to the leg's partner as a hop (a settlement line to the partner_transit receiver) within custody_max_hours; the custody view reports it with age. COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT.own_wallet_id may name a bridge as well as an own desk. New view WALLET_REGISTRY(network, address): every known address with its owner and role — partner wallets with risk band, NPL's wallets by role, receivers' wallets with their approvals, screened sender addresses with their decision — the FRS 'wallet registry', as a view over the four tables rather than a second copy.

Rejected alternative. Treating the bridge collection as a reroute each time; a stored registry table.

Why. NPL: partners have designated wallets for senders who cannot be screened up front, and where a partner lacks a network (Ali has no ERC-20) NPL collects on its own alternate wallet and forwards on a supported network, without the risk exposure. As written, invariant 3 forbade that routine flow. The FRS wallet registry had no single home.

D41 — Cash settlement evidence; recommend, then approve

Decision. SETTLEMENT_LINE.token_ref is the receiver's token, provided up front and relayed to the agent; the line gains evidence_ref, the agent's photo of the token after hand-over, relayed back to the receiver, whose confirmation closes the loop. COLLECTION.token_ref may be replaced by the partner before hand-over (a new agent), with the rate locked at quote unchanged. FEE_DECISION gains recommended_by (Finance) beside approved_by (Management) and APPROVAL gains cover_bank_fee and raise_fee_cap: a covered bank fee, or a markup above the cap after discussing with the customer, is reviewed by Finance and approved by Management. A partner rate below the limit warns and never refuses a quote. AED cash rounds to 100, USD cash in Dubai to 10.

Rejected alternative. Finance approving fee concessions on its own, as the generic one-off fee decision allowed.

Why. NPL: on settlement the receiver provides the token and the agent photographs it; covering a fee needs Finance's review and Management's approval; NPL may go above 2 % on THB after talking to the customer, so the system warns and Management decides on the cap.

D45 — Extending a quote's validity, as often as needed; honouring an expired rate

Decision. Replaces D42. QUOTE_VALIDITY_EXTENSION: one row per request — from and to validity, reason, approver, approval — any number per leg, each moving DEAL.effective_valid_until and re-issuing the QUOTE_PACKAGE at the same price; Finance approves, Management is added when the new validity passes the partner's cutoff or the rate version's expiry. After expiry a new deal group is required; at the sender's request it may be priced on the earlier leg's market rate and partner rate version — rate_reused_from_deal_id, rate_override_reason, rate_override_approved_by, the approval honour_expired_rate — with the automated rate set aside and the grace drift limit not applied; the difference against the partner's actual rate posts to variance. Invariant 37 restated, invariant 39 new.

Rejected alternative. The once-only, within-grace extension of D42; refusing the original rate after expiry.

Why. NPL: an Evo sender may ask for a 1-hour quote to be held for 6 hours, in more than one request, and a sender whose quote has expired may still want the original rate — the system must allow that rate to be entered by hand on the new deal rather than refuse. The price of a leg stays write-once: the clock moves by approved rows, and the old rate is copied into a new leg on record, with its cost visible.

D37 — Names aligned with the FRS and NPL's words

Decision. Tables: DISBURSEMENT → SETTLEMENT (and _LINE, _RETURN; disburse_policy → settlement_policy); INTRODUCER → MARKUP_SHARE_PARTY, REFERRAL_RULE → MARKUP_SHARE_RULE, REFERRAL_ACCRUAL → MARKUP_SHARE_ACCRUAL, purpose REFERRAL_PAYABLE → SHARE_PAYABLE, ledger source Referral → MarkupShare, cost component referral merged into share; SETTLEMENT_REGISTRATION → DESTINATION_APPROVAL. Columns: sender_share_pct / receiver_share_pct → sender_pays_pct / receiver_pays_pct; floor_pct / cap_pct → min_markup_pct / max_markup_pct; displayed_fee_basis / displayed_fee_pct / displayed_source_rate → customer_facing_fee_basis / customer_facing_fee_pct / customer_facing_rate; partner_markup_pct → partner_fee_pct with partner_pricing values fee_on_market / fee_in_rate; rate_basis values market / agent_rate. Kept at NPL's request: COLLECTION_SENDING_ENTITY, COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT, CONVERSION.residual_in. Appendix A.1 carries the old names as aliases.

Rejected alternative. Keeping the technical names and showing NPL's words only as labels in the app and the documents.

Why. The FRS and NPL say settlement, not disbursement; NPL's fee table calls Jeton's rebate a 'referral commission', so 'referral' in the model pointed the wrong way and since D26 the party is usually a customer such as Raeen; NPL’s word for a registration is 'approved'; the column names are the phrases NPL used when it answered the fee outlines ('sender pays', 'max markup', 'customer-facing calculation', 'fee on top of market', 'agent rate'). The earlier editions of the dependent documents still use the old names until they are regenerated.

D33 — Same-currency pass-through stays in scope

Decision. A CURRENCY_PAIR may have the same currency on both sides; the leg converts at rate 1 so the sender and receiver fee parts are captured at conversion like on any pair.

Rejected alternative. Dropping the dormant Evolution bank-transfer products.

Why. NPL: the fee is still applied because the currency is collected and then settled separately.

Amendments of 9 October (same draft)

D15. NPL confirmed the PARTNER_ENTITY rename. D27. pct_of_partner_fee is retired; basis + pct carry the rebate rule. D29. The bank cutoff moves to PARTNER: it is the partner's clock, like its rate expiry and holiday calendar, whichever project uses it. Later the same day NPL added that the cutoff governs two events — locking the rate and initiating the outgoing bank settlement — on the pairs that rely on the banking channel, and that it can be extended (30–60 minutes, partner agrees) or closed early (Fridays, pre-holiday): PARTNER_CUTOFF_OVERRIDE holds those per-day or weekday changes, the effective cutoff is stamped as cutoff_at on the leg and on the settlement, and SETTLEMENT.execution_due_date mirrors the leg's conversion due date for bank rails. D30 stands as first drafted: the cash city is DEAL.cash_location and PARTNER_RATE_VERSION.location. An amendment making the city a side of the currency pair (a CASH_LOCATION table) was applied and then withdrawn the same day at NPL's request. Stale wording from before D23, D25 and D26 was corrected in the notes, walkthroughs, invariant 4 and the FRS reconciliation.

Earlier revisions — v5.0 to v5.2

D13 — No return group

Decision. sender_return and partner_transit receivers belong to no group. Attribution of a return or hop leg is inherited from its parent leg. Offsets are defined between a leg's attributed group and the group of a counterparty receiver.

Rejected alternative. A dedicated group of kind = return per project holding the sender_return receivers (ERD v4.0 §6; config schema rule "one default and one return group").

Why. Groups exist for entitlement and offset accounting; refund exclusion is a receiver-kind rule, not an entitlement rule, and RECEIVER.kind already enforces it. The return group (a) made every project have at least two groups, so the Understanding document's "a project with a single group never has an offset" was false by construction; (b) classified every refund as a cross-group payout under the v4.0 offset definition, triggering Management approval and offset aging; (c) left the return group's entitlement negative after each refund, breaking invariant 7, unless a reattribution path was added. Removing it restores the Understanding document's §3.3 and §6.3 wording without change. The return group entered during the v4.0 write-up; decision D3 of the review record relied on it and is amended there.

Changed tables

TableChange
RECEIVER_GROUP− kind. A group is a group; exactly one is_default per project (D13).
RECEIVERgroup_id required when kind = counterparty, null otherwise. sender_return and partner_transit receivers never appear on forward deals or allow lists (validation on kind) (D13).
DEALreceiver_group_id: set at quote on the first forward leg; a return leg inherits it from its parent leg, leg n of a route from leg n−1 (D13).
SETTLEMENT_LINEA line paying a group-less receiver debits the paying leg's group and is never an offset (D13).
RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT+ account_kind (bank / wallet); details_ref → bank_details_ref (bank accounts only); + network, + address (wallets only). Write-time rule: a bank account has bank_details_ref and a bank rail; a wallet has network and address and a crypto rail matching the network (D14).

D14 — Explicit wallet fields on receiving-entity accounts. Rejected: keeping wallet details inside the opaque details_ref. Why: the collection side already stored network and address explicitly; the payout side did not, so addresses could not be validated, checked against the rail, or queried across partners. Bank details stay external by reference, as before.

D15 — Partner entity and collection endpoint

Decision. FACILITATING_ENTITY is renamed PARTNER_ENTITY: the partner's legal vehicle whose name appears on paperwork, the mirror of RECEIVING_ENTITY on the client side. COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENTITY (bank-in) and WALLET (crypto-in) merge into one COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT table owned by a partner entity, with kind = bank / wallet and the field shape of RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT (rail required only on active bank endpoints, see D18). COLLECTION points at one endpoint (collection_receiving_endpoint_id, null for cash) instead of the hand-rolled endpoint_type + endpoint_id pair. NPL confirmed the rename on 9 October 2026; the FRS term "Facilitating Entity" stays in Appendix A.1.

Rejected alternative. Keeping two endpoint tables, one with a legal owner (wallets under a vehicle) and one without (bank accounts directly under the partner config).

Why. A bank account is always in some legal entity's name, so the v4.0 split left the schema unable to say which vehicle owns a bank-in account, while every wallet knew its owner. One endpoint table under the vehicle fixes the asymmetry, lets the system check that the account a sender paid into belongs to the vehicle stamped on the deal, removes a polymorphic pair from COLLECTION, and makes the partner side read exactly like the client side: config → entity → endpoint.

TableChange
PARTNER_ENTITYrenamed from FACILITATING_ENTITY; − bank_details_ref (moved to its endpoints).
COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINTnew; replaces COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENTITY and WALLET. partner_entity_id, kind (bank / wallet), currency, bank_details_ref (bank), network + address (wallet), status.
COLLECTIONendpoint_type + endpoint_id → collection_receiving_endpoint_id (null for cash).
DEALfacilitating_entity_id → partner_entity_id.
Invariant 6adds: a collection's endpoint must belong to the leg's partner entity.

v5.2 — decisions of the review of the v5.1 draft (8 October 2026)

D16 — Registration payout details follow the account's kind

Decision. DESTINATION_APPROVAL gains network and address (nullable). bank_details_ref ("as paid by this partner") is set only when the registered account's account_kind is bank; for a wallet account the registration carries the network and address as the partner registered them, and the bank field stays empty. The registration remains the partner's view of the destination; RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT remains NPL's.

Rejected alternative. Keeping a bank-only field on wallet registrations (the v5.1 shape).

Why. After D14 and D15 every other destination record is kind-aware; a wallet registration had no field that fitted, so an approved wallet destination either carried no details or carried an address in a field named for bank details. Storing the partner's copy also lets the system compare NPL's record with the partner's before paying to a wallet, where a wrong address is unrecoverable.

D17 — SETTLEMENT_LINE.deal_id

Decision. SETTLEMENT_LINE gains deal_id, a nullable foreign key to DEAL: required when the paid receiver is group-less (sender_return, partner_transit), optional on counterparty lines. New invariant 19. GROUP_ENTITLEMENT reads the paying leg's group from it.

Rejected alternative. Leaving the rule in prose ("a payout to a group-less receiver debits the paying leg's group").

Why. A SETTLEMENT pools many deals, and neither it nor its lines named one; the D13 rule and the view that depends on it could not be computed from stored columns, and invariant 7 could not be checked mechanically. The same column will carry the per-line discharge facts of the scenario in which a EUR invoice is paid in USDT in parts.

D18 — Nullable rail on COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT

Decision. The endpoint gains rail, nullable. Null means "not yet known", never "does not matter": a bank endpoint cannot become active — and no COLLECTION or payment instruction may reference it — until rail is set; a wallet endpoint may leave rail null (its network already names the road), and when rail is set on a wallet it must match network (mirrors D14).

Rejected alternative. A NOT NULL rail, which forces a guessed value when a partner sends incomplete details; or no rail at all (the v5.1 shape), which made the "same field shape as RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT" claim inexact.

Why. The road matters on the collection side as much as on the payout side: the same EUR account reachable by SEPA or SWIFT needs different instructions and arrives with different fees; local rails carry transaction limits (UPI caps, RTGS minimums); and a wrong rail recorded with confidence causes the failures a blank cannot.

D19 — Endpoint kind must match the leg's collection method

Decision. A write-time rule, added to invariant 6: a collection endpoint's kind must match the leg's collection_method — wallet for crypto-in, bank for bank-in, and cash-in has no endpoint.

Rejected alternative. None; the rule was missing.

Why. After D15 the fact "how does the money arrive" lives in two places — DEAL.collection_method and the endpoint's kind — and nothing stopped them disagreeing silently.

Changed tables (v5.2)

TableChange
DESTINATION_APPROVAL+ network, + address (wallet accounts only); bank_details_ref only when the account's kind is bank (D16).
SETTLEMENT_LINE+ deal_id — nullable FK to DEAL; required when the paid receiver is group-less, optional on counterparty lines (D17).
COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT+ rail — nullable; required before a bank endpoint becomes active; on a wallet, must match network when set (D18).
COLLECTIONNo column change: may reference only an active endpoint whose kind matches the leg's collection_method (D18, D19).

Views and invariants

ItemChange
GROUP_ENTITLEMENTSums client_net over converted legs of both types; a payout line debits the paid receiver's group (counterparty) or the group of the leg named by its deal_id (group-less receivers) — computable from stored columns (D13, D17).
OFFSETEntitlement − paid per group, arising only when a counterparty receiver is paid from a leg attributed to another group.
Invariant 6Adds: a collection's endpoint must belong to the leg's partner entity (D15); its kind must match the leg's collection_method (D19); a COLLECTION may reference only an active endpoint, and a bank endpoint is active only with rail set (D18).
Invariant 7Restated: return and hop legs preserve conservation by inheriting the parent leg's group; since v5.2 every payout line resolves to a group, so the invariant is checkable mechanically (D17).
Invariant 17Restated: offsets only between a leg's attributed group and a counterparty receiver's group; a single-group project never has an offset.
Invariant 18group_id iff kind = counterparty; forward legs and the allow list target counterparty groups and receivers only; return and hop legs inherit attribution.
Invariant 19New: a line paying a group-less receiver carries deal_id; the paying leg's group is a stored fact, never inferred (D17).

Editorial corrections in v5.2

  • Invariant 18's note now says the allow list targets counterparty groups and receivers, not receivers alone.
  • The D13 write-up no longer claims the return group appeared in no decision-record entry: decision D3 of the review record did place sender_return receivers in a return group; the record amends D3 and carries D13–D19.
  • The dependent-documents table is refreshed: the data file is already erd.v5.json and the decision record carries D13–D19.
  • The third v5.1 change (D15) is dated 8 October 2026; this baseline is an internal New XP document from which the client deliverables are derived.
