9FRS figure reconciliation (1,208 vs 1,225; Mode 1 example)Golden casesNPL: Needs clarification. To be discussed.

Answered and reflected in v5.7

#QuestionAnswerIn the model
1Collect-first: must SENDER_RECEIVER_ALLOW pre-exist for attribution; handling of inbound matching no senderNPL: Yes, sender-receiver mapping should be done in configuration. When the transaction is created, the sender is picked from a list.v4.0: write-time rule that a collect-first deal needs an existing allow entry; the allow list now targets receiver groups.
2Withholding-eligibility criteria on rerouted dealsReview (7 Oct): NPL’s cut is always captured at conversion, so it is never at risk from a return or a forward. If forwarding happens before conversion, whichever partner converts captures it.v4.0: the eligibility question dissolves. forwarding_policy is forward_full or forward_and_recover_dues; withhold_earnings is removed. Ownership flips at one event only.
3Post-collection reroute (funds stuck at a partner): transfer, offset, or refund-and-requoteNPL: The partner can send the funds to NPL (and NPL decides where to send) or the partner can refund the sender.v4.0: REROUTE.outcome via_own_wallet / refund_sender; a refund is a return leg paying the sender_return receiver.
4Receiving-entity constraints (currency, rail) narrowing settlement choiceNPL: Receiving entities have specific bank accounts with currency and rail restrictions, for example EUR via SWIFT and EUR via SEPA.v4.0: RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT; registrations and payout lines point at the account.
5Any deliberate partial-settlement / reserve policyNPL: Yes, possible. In some projects the client’s funds sit until they are ready to receive them, within an exposure threshold NPL sets by appetite.v4.0: PROJECT.settlement_policy to_zero / hold_allowed with exposure_ceiling as the cap; invariant 4 restated.
6Receiver-side fee timing per projectNPL: Receiver-side fee should be applied at the time of conversion, otherwise the balance will be incorrect.v4.0: default at_conversion; CONVERSION.fee_receiver_part; SETTLEMENT_LINE.receiver_fee_applied becomes exceptional.
7Network-fee policy on refundsNPL: Set at project level with per-transaction override (one 100 USD fee was repaid in the next settlement).v4.0: PROJECT.network_fee_policy plus FEE_DECISION for the override.
8Whole-unit conversion rounding ruleReview (7 Oct): fractions are dropped to whole units at conversion, per transaction (30.152 → 30). The dropped fraction stays client money, carried in the balance and paid out when it reaches a whole unit. Cash collections round to the nearest 100 / 500 / 1000 by currency.v4.0: CONVERSION.rounding_residual; CURRENCY_PAIR.amount_rounding and cash_rounding_unit; settle to less than one unit; SHORTFALL no longer takes rounding. Superseded in v5.3 by D25: a rounding menu per pair, signed residual, EXP_ROUNDING for round-ups.
10AQN-LT-Sub “settled by offset against transactions outside the system”NPL: This is NPL’s wallet (pass-through at collection or on the settlement side). AQN is Aquanow, a crypto exchange; LT Sub is the account name.v4.0: OWN_WALLET.provider and account_label; pass-through is a two-leg route or a reroute via the own wallet.
11Reference workbooks per project archetypeFee Outlines v0.2 (8 October 2026): every line of NPL’s fee table as a fill-in outline with a worked calculation per transaction pattern, answered by NPL with the Project Context and Payment methods tabs.v5.3: decisions D20–D33 were built from it; the workbook is the acceptance reference for the fee engine.
12FRS P1 / P3 vs rerouting and multi-partner use — amend FRS or restrict scopeNPL: Check the added explanations (partner types and channels; pass-through and double conversions in §7.1.1). Ask again if still unclear.v4.0: two-leg routes are deal groups with two legs and a partner_transit receiver for the hop; FRS principles generalised, scope kept.
13Advance funding sourceReview (7 Oct): never. NPL does not pay a receiver before the client’s money has arrived.v4.0: LEDGER_ACCOUNT purpose ADVANCE removed; the advance approval and the “advance” ownership-flip event removed.
14Review point: entitlement split on a balance conversionReview (7 Oct): chosen group, not proportional. The conversion is triggered by a specific payout.v4.0: BALANCE_CONVERSION.receiver_group_id; excess over the group’s source-currency entitlement is booked as an approved offset.
15Review point: refunds to a third party at the sender’s requestReview (7 Oct): allowed by exception only. Default is the sender’s own return receiver; any other destination needs Management approval with a reason and a pre-registered approved receiver.v4.0: invariant on return legs; APPROVAL action refund_to_third_party.
16Review point: recover dues on a rerouteReview (7 Oct): yes, NPL nets what a partner owes it against funds about to be forwarded to that partner.v4.0: forwarding_policy forward_and_recover_dues, recovered_amount, partner_agreement_ref; postings own wallet cash ← earnings receivable, no income.
17Review point: legs of a route share one client-facing quoteReview (7 Oct): yes, a deal group. The sender saw one price and one reference; margin across legs is the group quote minus the partner conversions.v4.0: DEAL_GROUP; every deal belongs to a group, a single-partner deal being a group of one leg.
18Review point (v5.0): does a refund need its own receiver group?Review (7 Oct, New XP): No. Refund exclusion is a receiver-kind rule; a dedicated return group made every project multi-group (so “a single-group project never has an offset” was false by construction), classified every refund as a cross-group offset needing Management approval, and left its entitlement negative after each refund, breaking invariant 7.v5.0 (D13): sender_return and partner_transit receivers are group-less; return and hop legs inherit the parent leg’s attribution; offsets are defined only against counterparty groups. New invariant 18.
19Review point (v5.1): restructure the partner collection side — rename FACILITATING_ENTITY, merge the endpoints?Review (8 Oct, New XP): yes. A bank account is always in some legal entity’s name, so the v4.0 split could not say which vehicle owned a bank-in account while every wallet knew its owner. The rename to PARTNER_ENTITY was confirmed by NPL on 9 October 2026; the FRS keeps “Facilitating Entity”.D15: FACILITATING_ENTITY → PARTNER_ENTITY (bank_details_ref moved to its endpoints); COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENTITY and WALLET merge into COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT (kind bank / wallet, same shape as RECEIVING_ENTITY_ACCOUNT); COLLECTION points at one endpoint (null for cash); invariant 6 adds that a collection’s endpoint must belong to the leg’s partner entity.
20Review point (v5.3): can the model express NPL’s fee practice as described in the fee table, NPL’s workbook answers and the Project Context / Payment methods tabs (gaps A–M)?NPL (8–9 Oct): all thirteen confirmed with parameters — receiver part fixed (A); calendar-month tiers, a crossing deal split across tiers (B); displayed 1 % is a BF-only rule (C); run NPL-GR inside NPLify as an own desk (D); invoice tracking wanted (E); rounding menu, round up to 1,000 for Asian currencies (F); markup shared = fee − partner fee, several parties, party holds the funds, rebate NPL’s alone (G); rebates reported apart, statement covers NPLify deals only (H); Ali quotes inverted (I); NPL absorbs the next-day rate difference, pending converted value shown from the lock (J); cash by token, rates by city (K); screening is an Operations action (L); losses partial and shared, both sides, any method (M); same-currency pass-through stays in scope.v5.3, D20–D33: FEE_TIER, DEAL_FEE_TIER, INVOICE, WALLET_SCREENING, LOSS_EVENT; views INVOICE_BALANCE, PROJECT_MONTH_VOLUME; invariants 20–32 and invariant 3 restated; purposes EARN_REBATE, SHARE_RECEIVABLE, EXP_ROUNDING, EXP_LOSS.
21Review point (v5.3): four FRS terms with no home in the ERD — wallet registry, holiday calendar, message template, quote package.Review (9 Oct, NPL + New XP): wallet registry = COLLECTION_RECEIVING_ENDPOINT of kind wallet (D15). The other three are added: the holiday calendar was a label and could not drive ‘next business day’; the quote package is the evidence behind priced-once and the quote clocks; the template is where the sender-facing-only rule on messages is enforced.v5.3 D34 HOLIDAY, D35 QUOTE_PACKAGE, D36 MESSAGE_TEMPLATE; invariants 33–34; quote-first walkthrough gains the package step.
22Review point (v5.4): project = client made client-level reporting impossible when one client runs several arrangements (BF, BF Sub, BF Withdrawal; 66 Group in remittance and in the game reseller).NPL (9 Oct): add a parent clients table. New XP: yes — CLIENT above PROJECT with a roll-up view; parties stay per project for now (a shared sender registry can be added later without breaking attribution).v5.4 D38: CLIENT (name, category, legal entity, KYC, relationship owner, optional exposure ceiling); PROJECT.client_id; CLIENT_POSITION view; invariant 35.
23Review point (v5.4): NPL’s answers to the operational questions of the scenario catalogue — alternate wallets, partner methods, cutoff scope, cash settlement token, fee cover, local deposits.NPL (9 Oct, evening): partners have designated wallets for unscreened senders and NPL bridges unsupported networks on its own wallet; a partner’s methods are configuration; the cutoff exists only for Ali-type partners and only on bank-side pairs; on a cash payout the receiver issues the token and the agent photographs it; a cash deposit into a bank account is a local payment; Finance recommends and Management approves fee concessions.v5.4 D39 PARTNER.supported_methods, cutoff nullable, invariant 36; D40 OWN_WALLET.role / networks, invariant 3 restated, WALLET_REGISTRY view; D41 SETTLEMENT_LINE.evidence_ref, FEE_DECISION.recommended_by, approval actions cover_bank_fee and raise_fee_cap.
24Review point (v5.4): a system currency for reporting — aggregated collection volumes, earnings and balances across currencies, per project or overall.NPL (9 Oct): a display layer that converts each currency figure at the current market rate into one reporting currency, for project-specific or overall volumes, earnings and current balances; estimated figures.v5.4 D43: SYSTEM_SETTING (reporting_currency, reporting_rate_source, reporting_rate_max_age_min, operating_timezone); system reporting CURRENCY_PAIRs with no project; REPORTING_VALUE view; invariant 38; CLIENT.exposure_ceiling stated in the reporting currency.
25Review point (v5.7): the ledger design — accrual timing, loss events, the NPL-GR reseller P&L, variance accounts, earnings kept unconverted and offset between partners, money in transit, fee arithmetic.NPL (10–11 Oct): accrue shares and rebates at conversion; book a loss to NPL first and recover share by share; run NPL-GR’s full reseller P&L inside NPLify with two invoices in EUR and the remittance markup absorbing partner cost and forex; one variance account per cause; earnings taken out of unconverted collections and offset between partners at the partner’s rate of the day; sent money is not NPL’s — the promise is discharged on release; bank transfers carry cents, cash rounds; fee parts on the principal; Jeton 1.25 %, Ali assumed 1 %; EUR → EUR 2.8 % split 50/50; NPL’s profit = remittance + reseller earnings.v5.7 D46: LEDGER_ACCOUNT purposes (VAR_ × 4, LOSS_RECEIVABLE, MAKEGOOD, LOSS_PAYABLE, RESELL_REVENUE, RESELL_COST, VENDOR_PAYABLE, RESALE_RECEIVABLE, REMIT_CLAIM, FX_CLEARING; INTRANSIT retired), sources LossRecovery / Invoice / EarningsOffset, component resale; LOSS_RECOVERY and EARNINGS_OFFSET tables; INVOICE.kind, sender_id; EARNINGS_RECEIVABLE.recovered_by_offset_id; PARTNER_REBATE_RULE.payout_currency; CURRENCY_PAIR.amount_rounding exact; views RESELLER_MARGIN, REMITTANCE_MARGIN, NPL_PROFIT; invariants 16, 25, 26, 28, 39 restated, 40–44 new.
